sentence: This project studies how prostate cancer becomes lethal after it turns resistant to castration, using patient datasets and patient-derived models.
This project builds a computer framework that tries to find out how protein mutations cause diseases or drug resistance.
This project uses 3D printing to build scaffolds and tests how their features affect stem cell therapy for brain cancer after surgery.
This project builds an imaging tool that pairs a compact device with an ultrasound scanner to show targeting agents in a patient in real time.
This project studies what drives stem-like tumor cells to form in basal-like breast cancer.
This project builds computer and lab methods to find which genetic variants cause cardiovascular disease and which genes they control.
This project studies how retinal ganglion cells change as the retina degenerates, so they can be controlled with an electronic retinal implant.
This project studies whether repeat elements in the genome help pancreatic and gastroesophageal cancer cells resist chemoradiation.
This project studies how a key protein and its partner drive breast cancer growth, stem cell formation, spread and treatment resistance.
This project uses mouse methods such as imaging and MRI to study how reactive astrocytes affect blood flow, metabolism and neuron activity.
This project uses pet dogs getting cancer treatment to study clonal hematopoiesis, a precancerous blood state that dogs develop naturally.
This project strengthens biomedical research infrastructure to build a lasting culture of research.
This project studies how exercise changes immune function and affects immunotherapy results and side effects in patients with lung cancer.
This project builds computer models of learning and studies the roles of the prefrontal cortex and striatum in learning from many features.
This project studies how psychosocial stress, through changes in the vaginal microbiome, contributes to advanced ovarian cancer.
This project studies the genetic and epigenetic mechanisms behind how cancer starts and progresses, using animal model systems.
This project studies how bacteria fight off bacteriophage infections, so that bacteriophages can kill bacteria more effectively.
This project builds a tool that reads RNA molecules one at a time, including their chemical modifications, using tiny devices and enzymes.
This project builds computer tools that use sequencing data to predict what each T-cell receptor binds.
This project studies how the immune system interacts with antibodies delivered by viral vectors to prevent HIV transmission.
